question: Which two main blood vessel systems supply oxygenated blood to the brain?
explanation: Great job! The internal carotid arteries supply the front of the brain, while the vertebral arteries supply the back. Together, they keep the brain well-nourished with oxygen. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the main job of the Circle of Willis at the base of the brain?

options.A: To drain deoxygenated blood away from the cerebral cortex
options.B: To cool down the blood before it reaches delicate brain tissue
options.C: To provide alternative blood supply routes if a vessel is blocked
options.D: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the central nervous system

explanation: Spot on! The Circle of Willis acts like a backup traffic network. If one path gets blocked, it reroutes blood so the brain keeps getting what it needs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h1)

question: What directly causes an ischemic stroke?

options.A: A sudden drop in systemic body temperature
options.B: A ruptured blood vessel inside the brain
options.C: An infection of the cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: A blood clot blocking a cerebral artery

explanation: You got it! Ischemic strokes happen when a clot cuts off blood flow to a part of the brain, starving those cells of oxygen. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h2)

question: How does a hemorrhagic stroke cause damage to the brain?

options.A: By causing bleeding that increases pressure and compresses brain cells
options.B: By causing a permanent lack of glucose without altering pressure
options.C: By replacing normal neurons with fibrous scar tissue over time
options.D: By triggering widespread bacterial growth in the ventricles

explanation: Spot on! When a blood vessel bursts inside the skull, the pooling blood builds up pressure and squeezes the surrounding delicate brain tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which of these is the most common and controllable risk factor for having a stroke?
explanation: Correct! High blood pressure puts constant, dangerous strain on the brain's blood vessels, making it the number one risk factor we can manage. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h3)

question: A 55-year-old patient has a 10-year history of poorly controlled high blood pressure. What major condition are they at high risk for?
explanation: You nailed it! Years of high pressure wear down cerebral blood vessels, putting the patient at high risk for a stroke (cerebrovascular accident). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h3)

question: In the FAST stroke assessment tool, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
explanation: Correct! 'A' stands for arm weakness. We check if one arm drifts downward when the patient tries to hold both arms up. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h4)

question: If a patient has a stroke on the right side of their motor cortex, which side of the body will show physical weakness?
explanation: Brilliant! Brain pathways cross over in the brainstem, so damage on the right side of the brain shows up as weakness on the left side of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why must an emergency CT scan be done immediately for a suspected stroke patient?

options.C: To calculate total intracranial blood volume
options.D: To measure electrical brain wave activity

explanation: Spot on! We need to check if the stroke is caused by bleeding. Giving clot-busting medications during a hemorrhagic stroke would be deadly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why does a nurse check blood clotting test results before giving clot-dissolving therapy to a stroke patient?

options.A: To confirm the exact age and size of the blood clot in the vessel
options.B: To ensure the patient does not have an unsafe risk of severe bleeding
options.C: To check if the patient has an active urinary tract infection
options.D: To measure the patient's baseline neurological recovery potential

explanation: Correct! These drugs are powerful. We must make sure the patient's clotting profile is safe so they don't suffer severe, uncontrollable bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using clot-busting (thrombolytic) therapy in an acute ischemic stroke?

options.A: To prevent future heart attacks from occurring
options.B: To dissolve the blood clot and restore blood flow
options.C: To lower systemic blood pressure instantly
options.D: To shrink swollen brain tissue caused by edema

explanation: You got it! Thrombolytic therapy breaks down the clot blocking the vessel, getting oxygen flowing back to starving brain cells quickly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the purpose of an endovascular thrombectomy procedure?

options.A: Physically remove a large blood clot from a blocked cerebral artery
options.B: Surgically repair a ruptured blood vessel inside the brain
options.C: Drain excess cerebrospinal fluid from the lateral ventricles
options.D: Bypass a narrowed carotid artery using a synthetic graft

explanation: Spot on! During a thrombectomy, doctors use specialized tools threaded through blood vessels to physically grab and pull out large clots. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h6)

question: What crucial nursing check must be done before giving food or water to a stroke patient who might have trouble swallowing?

options.D: A complete neurological Glasgow Coma Scale score

explanation: Correct! Swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) can easily lead to aspiration pneumonia. A bedside swallow screen keeps the patient safe before any oral intake. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h7)

question: For a stroke patient with left-sided weakness who is confined to bed, what is the best nursing action to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat at all times
options.B: Repositioning the patient every two hours and supporting weak limbs
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Massaging the reddened bony prominences vigorously every shift

explanation: You nailed it! Turning the patient regularly relieves pressure on vulnerable skin, while supporting weak limbs protects their joints. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h7)

question: A stroke patient is resting in bed for a long time without moving. What major leg complication are they most at risk for?
explanation: Spot on! When a patient cannot move well, blood pools in the lower legs, putting them at high risk for deep vein thrombosis (DVT). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h8)

question: What is the main goal of secondary stroke prevention strategies?

options.A: To prevent a recurrent stroke by managing underlying risk factors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any ongoing physical therapy
options.C: To reverse existing brain cell death and restore lost tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying genetic cause of high blood pressure

explanation: Brilliant! Secondary prevention is all about keeping lifestyle habits in check, taking medications properly, and managing blood pressure to stop another stroke from happening. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h8)
